items.title: Build the web shell with session parity, security headers and the money primitive
items.outcome: The web application has an authenticated shell whose session rules match mobile exactly, a strict content policy and request forgery defence, and a money type that makes a floating point amount impossible to compile.
items.context: The web epic is the second place a user sees their financial position, and the two most common ways to get it wrong are a token in browser storage and a floating point amount in a chart. Both are prevented at the shell layer or not at all.
scope: Session handling with secure, same-site, http-only cookies and refresh rotation matching the server rules
Reuse detection handling that signs the user out with an explanation
Nonce-based content security policy with no inline script allowance
Request forgery protection on every state-changing route
Money type in TypeScript wrapping integer minor units with a currency
Static analysis rule failing the build when a money field is typed as a plain number
Locale-aware rendering at the render boundary only, defaulting to INR presentation
Discoverable privacy-safe help and support entry from signed-out, signed-in and error states
Web registration, channel verification and account recovery journeys implementing the published T-AUTH-01 contract, including the cooling-off and cancellation states
acceptance_criteria: No authentication token is reachable from browser script storage, proven by a test
A refresh token reuse revokes the session family and the user is told why
The content policy blocks an injected inline script in a test page
A state-changing request without a valid token is rejected
A deliberate floating point amount fails the build
Formatting happens only at the render boundary; the domain layer contains no formatted strings
Security headers are asserted by an automated test rather than reviewed by eye
Help is keyboard reachable without authentication and any diagnostic bundle excludes money, message content, provider keys and credentials
A user can register, verify their channel and complete account recovery entirely on the web, using only the published contract
The web recovery journey shows the cooling-off window and offers cancellation, and never describes recovery as instant
Registration and recovery responses reveal nothing about whether an account exists, in body, status or timing band
contracts_schema: Consumes the generated TypeScript client for the published authentication contract and money representation
security_privacy: No secret reaches the client bundle, enforced by the scaffold check
Error output never includes tokens or amounts
observability: Client errors reported with scrubbed payloads and no monetary values
tests: Storage inspection test
Reuse detection test
Policy and header assertion tests
Planted floating point build failure test
Signed-out help navigation, keyboard access and planted-sensitive-value diagnostic scrub tests
Web registration, verification and recovery journey tests
Account enumeration test across the web registration and recovery routes
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind an internal access gate until the quality gate passes
Rollback removes the public entry point; no user data is affected
non_goals: Feature screens, which are the other web tickets
Administrative functionality, which lives in a separate repository
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo web. Owns the shell, session client and money type. Server behaviour is consumed through the published contract only.

items.title: Build web transactions, bulk edit, statement import and full data export
items.outcome: As a user on a large screen, I can manage accounts, categories and individual transactions, work through thousands of records quickly, reconcile cash and refunds, import with a preview, and export complete data that imports back cleanly.
items.context: Bulk work and export are the reasons the web application exists; they are painful on a phone. Export in particular is a trust commitment: a product that asks for message access must make leaving easy and complete.
scope: Virtualised transaction list that stays responsive at large record counts
Bulk edit applied as a single idempotent batch operation
Statement import with column mapping and a dry-run preview before commit
Full export in both a tabular and a structured format, covering every user-owned entity
Export gated behind step-up authentication and rate limited
Progress, cancellation and result reporting for long-running operations
Access-log and account-deletion surfaces with reauthentication, request status and irreversible-action confirmation
Export, consent and rights-request surfaces built on the versioned shapes published by T-CON-09 rather than a web-only schema
Create, edit and archive accounts through the published account contract, with balances always server-derived
Create and correct individual transactions and category splits through the idempotent transaction API
Cash reconciliation and refund review using T-CON-13, including pending, offline, stale, conflict and correction states
acceptance_criteria: The list stays within the published interaction budget at ten thousand records
A bulk edit is one batch call carrying an idempotency key and a retry produces no duplicate change
Nothing is written until the user commits from the import preview and re-importing the same file creates no duplicates
An export re-imports into an empty account and produces an equivalent dataset, verified by a round-trip test
Export without a fresh step-up proof is refused
A cancelled import or export leaves no partial state
A user can inspect access events about themselves and cannot access another user's event
Account deletion requires recent reauthentication, shows progress and reports completion only after the erasure workflow verifies it
Export offers the versioned CSV and JSON formats published by T-CON-09 and shows the format version; a web-only export shape fails contract verification
A keyboard-only user can create an account, enter and split a transaction, reconcile cash and relink a refund without client-side money arithmetic
A correction creates the published reversing relation and never mutates ledger history
Pending or failed refunds are never rendered as settled income, and a cash withdrawal is shown as a transfer rather than spending
contracts_schema: Uses the published transactions, import and export contracts; export format is versioned and documented
security_privacy: Export is one of the highest value targets for a stolen session, so step-up and rate limiting are mandatory
Export files are delivered over an expiring link and are not retained beyond the published window
Deletion and access-log views never expose another subject and never claim completion before server verification
observability: Export and import events record counts and outcomes only, never content
tests: Round-trip export and import equivalence test
Bulk edit idempotency test
Step-up refusal test
Large list interaction budget test
Cross-user access-log denial test
Reauthentication, deletion progress and verified-completion end-to-end tests
Account, manual transaction and category-split keyboard and screen-reader journeys
Cash reconciliation and refund relink contract journeys
rollout_rollback: Export ships behind a flag until the round-trip test is green in staging
Rollback disables the export entry point; previously issued links expire normally
non_goals: Server import parsing, which the api import ticket owns
Administrative bulk export, which is deliberately a different, gated path

items.title: Build the web debt dashboard, strategy comparison and derivation inspector with budgets and reporting
items.outcome: As a user, I can see my payoff position, compare strategies, simulate extra payments and open any derived number to see exactly where it came from, alongside budgets and reporting for analysis.
items.context: The product promise is that a user can see why a payoff date is what it is. That is only credible if the client never recomputes anything and every number expands into its inputs, which is also the defence against a client and server disagreeing.
scope: Payoff dashboard sourced entirely from server computations
Strategy comparison across the supported strategies with the assumptions shown
Extra-payment simulator that states what it assumed
Derivation inspector expanding any derived figure into its inputs and formula
Budgets, categories and reporting views for analysis
Empty, partial and error states for every surface
acceptance_criteria: No derived monetary figure is computed in client code, enforced by review and by a static check on the money module
Every derived figure on screen can be expanded to its inputs and the computation identifier
Strategy comparison shows the assumptions used and refuses to display a comparison when the inputs are infeasible
Charts read from the same server values as the tables and cannot disagree with them
Reporting views render correctly with no data, with one record and with a large history
Monetary values carry accessible labels so a screen reader announces them unambiguously
contracts_schema: Consumes the published debt, strategy, simulation and budget contracts including the derivation fields
security_privacy: Screens are export-safe: no monetary value reaches an analytics payload
Computation identifiers are opaque and reveal nothing about other users
observability: View events record surface and outcome only, never amounts
tests: Derivation expansion test per derived figure
Chart and table consistency test
Empty, single and large dataset rendering tests
Accessibility announcement test
rollout_rollback: Ships behind a flag per surface so an incorrect derivation can be withdrawn without removing the dashboard
Rollback hides the affected surface and shows an explanatory state rather than a stale number
non_goals: Engine implementation, which the api debt tickets own
Goal planning surfaces, which belong to E22
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo web. Owns the dashboard, comparison and reporting surfaces. All arithmetic stays on the server.

items.title: Build the web support intake and request status surface
items.outcome: A web user can raise a support request, attach permitted evidence, follow its status against the published response target, and reach it from every help entry point in the product, so no help link points at an unowned mailbox.
items.context: Help and contact links already appear in the web billing, trust and onboarding surfaces and resolve to nothing owned. Web is also where a user goes when the app itself is the problem, which makes it the surface that must work when the Android client cannot, including for a user who cannot sign in.
scope: Request creation with category selection and the response target shown before submission
Attachment upload within the permitted types, sizes and expiry, with the rule stated at the point of upload
Request list and detail with the status, the thread and the remaining response time
Unauthenticated intake path for a user who cannot sign in, with the reduced capability that implies
Replacement of every existing help and contact entry point in the web product with a link to this surface
Applicable states from the T-UX-01 taxonomy on every screen
acceptance_criteria: A request can be created, its status followed and messages added, using only the published contract
The response target shown to the user is the value the server returns, including the priority-support variant, and is never computed in the client
An attachment outside the permitted types or size is refused in the client with the reason, and the server refusal is handled without data loss in the form
The unauthenticated intake path works without a session and clearly states what it cannot do, and it never reveals whether an account exists for an entered address
Every help or contact entry point in the web product resolves to this surface; a link to an unowned mailbox or an external form fails review
Every applicable T-UX-01 state identifier is handled, asserted by the client state coverage check
The surface meets the same accessibility budget as the rest of the web product
contracts_schema: Consumes the support shapes published by T-CON-11 through the generated TypeScript client
security_privacy: The form rejects credentials, session tokens and recovery codes before submission and explains why
The unauthenticated path is rate limited and gives an identical response whether or not the address matches an account
No support content is cached in the browser beyond the session
observability: Submission, abandonment and attachment-refusal rates are recorded so a confusing form is visible
tests: Request creation and status journey test
Attachment refusal test
Unauthenticated intake enumeration test
Help-entry-point link audit test
State coverage test against the T-UX-01 identifiers
rollout_rollback: Ships behind a flag with the existing help links redirected only once intake is live
Rollback restores the previous links, which is why the previous destination is recorded rather than deleted
non_goals: Support service, triage and vendor integration, which T-SUP-01 owns
Android support surfaces, which T-SUP-02 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo web. Owns the intake form, the request list and detail, and the help entry points in the web product. The service, the vendor adapter and the verification endpoint belong to T-SUP-01.
